findings.issue: Body-candidate position is only tested at beta=0; the aberrated-position claim (StarLight.apparent_direction at speed) has no test, so dropping the call would still pass.

Ship occlusion ray uses projected point clamped to the viewport; a body whose centre is off-screen but disc visible is tested at a clamped point. Minor. Occlusion by ship is untested for bodies (only catalogue stars).

Distant filter (kind!=star, radius_px<.5, dist>1000 AU) is sensible: own-system planets (<1000 AU, e.g. Neptune ~30 AU) stay offered, stars always offered. Nothing visible hidden as far as read; no test asserts the filter (TRAPPIST-1 only checked via an inspected render).
Capture calls inspect_body() directly, not a click, so I3 renders do not prove click path at tour stops; Earth stop inspects the Sun, not Earth.
Card facts and units correct and tested (AU/ly/km, R-sun/Jupiter/Earth, apparent size, light age). Open in map only when info.records has the catalogue id (correct, but untested).
Perf: body loop is O(bodies) with per-body StarLight/occlusion calls; star loop is pre-existing O(eligible) with signature-cached samples. Not a regression; body work is uncached per update.
Opened Earth/Jupiter/TRAPPIST-1: warm rings on discs, card fits, facts plausible (Jupiter 142,984 km, 1.02 R-jup, 0.48 s light age).

click_precedence: Correct: a click inside a body disc returns only the nearest such body; stars beside it still resolve (tested).
notes: Evaluator did not run full make test or golden.
